p: this song be sung in the: This song was made to comfort the faithful when their captivity would come, assuring them also of their deliverance, for which they should sing this song.
salvation will God appoint for walls: God's protection and defence will be sufficient for us.
Open ye the gates: He assures the godly to return after the captivity to Jerusalem.
mind is stayed on thee: You have decreed so, and your purpose cannot be changed.
the lofty city: There is no power so high that it can hinder God, when he will deliver his.
poor: God will set the poor afflicted over the power of the wicked.
judgments: We have constantly abode in the adversities with which you had afflicted us.
righteousness: Meaning that by afflictions men will learn to fear God.
be shown to the wicked: The wicked though God show them evident signs of his grace, will not be any better off.
envy at the people: Through envy and indignation against your people.
enemies shall devour them: The fire and vengeance with which you destroy your enemies.
lords beside thee have had dominion: The Babylonians, who have not governed according to your word.
dead: Meaning that the reprobate even in this life will have the beginning of everlasting death.
the nation: That is, the company of the faithful by the calling of the Gentiles.
visited thee: That is, the faithful by the rods were moved to pray to you for deliverance.
sight: That is, in extreme sorrow.
wind: Our sorrows had no end, neither did we enjoy the comfort that we looked for.
the world fallen: The wicked and men without religion were not destroyed.

Thy dead men shall live: He comforts the faithful in their afflictions, showing them that even in death they will have life and that they would certainly rise to glory, the contrary would come to the wicked, as in Isa 26:14.
dew is as the dew of: As herbs dead in winter flourish again by the rain in the springtime, so they who lie in the dust will rise up to joy, when they feel the dew of God's grace.
enter thou into thy chambers: He exhorts the faithful to be patient in their afflictions and to wait on God's work.
blood: The earth will vomit and cast out the innocent blood, which it has drunk, that it may care for vengeance against the wicked.
